name: Emeline Hotel
positioning: Art- and music-filled hotel at 181 Church Street in historic downtown Charleston, just north of the open-air market
best_for: Travelers who want a walkable base in historic downtown Charleston
Art lovers drawn to the Charleston Renaissance and the nearby Gibbes Museum of Art
Guests who like playing vinyl records in their room

facts.text: The hotel is at 181 Church Street in Charleston.
The hotel sits just north of Charleston's historic open-air market.
The Gibbes Museum of Art is three blocks from the hotel.
Over the years, 181 Church Street housed a grocery business, a provisions company that supplied local hotels, restaurants and ships, and a bank.
The hotel is by Makeready, which worked with local maker Urban Electric on its light fixtures.
A circular iron staircase leads to a mezzanine balcony overlooking the entry.
The suite Condé Nast Traveler reviewed had a bathroom with a walk-in rain shower and travertine floors.
The lobby-level Keep Shop sells curated local collectibles.
Horse carriages can be caught right outside the hotel's front door.
The hotel's restaurant, Frannie & The Fox, has a menu designed around a central wood-fired oven and opens onto an inner courtyard with a fire.
A 'foxhole' speakeasy drink window gives hidden direct access to the bar.

highlights.text: Emeline's Archive is a curated collection celebrating the Charleston Renaissance, a period from 1920 through World War II.
Rooms have a Crosley turntable, and the hotel has a vinyl record collection for guests to play.
Bi-level townhouse-style 'masonette' rooms open onto the inner courtyard.
The hotel runs an artist-in-residency program to connect guests with the local art scene.
The hotel has beach cruiser bikes for pedaling around town.

considerations.text: The hotel is in a heavily touristed part of historic downtown Charleston, just north of the open-air market.
WhataHotel notes limited parking in the busy downtown area.
WhataHotel notes it can be noisy due to the central location.
